name: GSAP Spring Stagger
description: Sequenced GSAP timeline that staggers a row of elements in with back.out overshoot, eases a numeric counter alongside, holds, then exits with reverse stagger. The canonical case CSS keyframes can't express — multiple targets choreographed on one timeline with a custom ease and a non-DOM tween (counter) firing onUpdate per frame.

stagger_ms.description: Delay between each element's entrance (ms). Translates to GSAP's stagger value (seconds) as stagger_ms / 1000.

entrance_ease.description: GSAP ease string for the entrance tween. back.out gives the signature overshoot.

counter_target.description: Final value of the numeric counter tween.

hold_ms.description: Hold duration after entrance + counter complete, before exit begins (ms).

when_to_use: Multi-element entrances where the sequence itself carries meaning (e.g. cards revealing one-by-one with overshoot)
Scenes that combine DOM motion with a numeric tween (counter, progress) on the same timeline
Cinematic-dark hero moments that need a custom ease beyond CSS cubic-bezier
when_to_avoid: Single-element transitions — the timeline orchestration is overkill
Scenes that need React-tree composition — use lib-framer-spring-stagger instead
Neutral-light tutorials — back.out overshoot reads too kinetic for the tutorial register
ai_guidance: First library-driven compound primitive. The capture pipeline auto-attaches the GSAP adapter (disables lagSmoothing, uncaps ticker.fps) when window.gsap is present. ESM prototypes that import gsap from a bundler must call window.__animaticSyncGsap?.(gsap) once after import — it's a no-op outside capture mode. The prototype_template demonstrates the full pattern.
